text:
cheng: Quick heads-up, onboarding a HF checkpoint and the converted Redwood config ended up with a silent kv-cache shift. evals show a big quality hit after quant.

sasha: what do you mean by "kv-cache shift"? mismatch in num_key_value_heads? :thinking_face:

dan: if num_kv_heads mismatch, models can still run but attention maps get scrambled -> hallucinations. did you check max_position_embeddings too?

cheng: yes. checkpoint had num_key_value_heads=32, converted config.json had 16. also sliding_window was true in HF, but our converter turned it into a sliding_window window_size that effectively clipped tokens earlier. snippet:

```
// from converted config.json
"num_key_value_heads": 16,
"max_position_embeddings": 2048,
"rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "factor": 1.05},
"sliding_window": true,
"sliding_window_size": 1024
```

heidi: oof. checkpoint metadata shows num_kv_heads: 32 and max_pos 4096?

cheng: exact. the HF model's config.json (from repo) has max_position_embeddings: 4096 and sliding_window: false (they rely on dynamic kv). When we set sliding_window_size=1024 we truncated the live kv indices and the rope scaling got applied differently -> quantization exacerbated error.

sasha: did you run the quantized eval vs fp16? numbers?

cheng: yep. fp16 eval perplexity on long-context eval set ~ 11.9. post-conversion int8 perf -> 28.4. short-context still OK (~12.5 -> 14.1). long-context failures match token-shift pattern.

dan: any diffs in tokenizer special tokens? chat_template mismatches can change offsets and cause off-by-one token alignment with kv cache.

cheng: there was one: HF had "<|user|>", "<|assistant|>" but our chat_template mapped them to user: "<|usr|>". converter tried to normalize but missed the pair. So tokenization + kv head mismatch + sliding_window created a 1-2 token drift that cascades.

heidi: can you repro minimal case? like generate with same prompt and dump attention maps / kv indices.

cheng: repro script attached inline:

```
# minimal repro (run in container)
python tools/repro_kv_shift.py \
  --model hf-checkpoint/ \
  --converted-config converted/config.json \
  --prompt "USER: repeat 200 tokens of A" \
  --dump-kv kv_dump.npz
```

sasha: 👍 run that on quant and fp16 and diff the kv shapes/values. also post the config from the HF repo for comparison.

cheng: did that. attached diffs show kv shape mismatch: fp16 kv heads: (layers, seq, 32, head_dim) vs converted: (layers, seq, 16, head_dim). reassembly code silently reshaped which messed the key ordering.

ci-bot: conversion-runner: job #4821 completed with non-fatal warnings: detected head_count_mismatch. See /ci/logs/4821

dan: converter should fail loudly on head mismatches. filed a tiny PR to add strict validation and preserve HF sliding_window false -> Redwood will not set sliding_window_size unless explicitly present.

heidi: also add a check that rope_scaling only applies when max_position_embeddings matches or when user explicitly accepts scaling fallback.

sasha: for short-term hotfix: (1) set num_key_value_heads to 32 in converted config, (2) copy HF max_position_embeddings=4096, (3) align chat_template special tokens. that'll restore fp16 parity, then rerun int8 quant.

cheng: doing that now. will post results. thanks!

dan: great. also add an integration test that loads HF metadata and flags silent mismatches during conversion.

cheng: agree. creating smoke test ticket.

sasha: filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGML-1248 with repro + logs. tagging @eng-releases for next patch.

cheng: patch applied locally. int8 long-context perplexity back to ~13.2. still slightly worse than fp16 but within expected quant gap. closing interim triage. :tada:

heidi: nice work. let's make the converter stricter and add chat_template validation to avoid this class of regressions.

cheng: will follow up with PR to restore stricter checks + add E2E long-context eval to CI.
